topicTitle: Important aspects of governance, transparency and accountability

syllabusMapping.prelims: Indian Polity and Governance - Constitution, Political System, Panchayati Raj, Public Policy, Rights Issues, etc.
syllabusMapping.mains: GS Paper II: Important aspects of governance, transparency and accountability, e-governance- applications, models, successes, limitations, and potential; citizens charters, transparency & accountability and institutional and other measures.

prelimsCapsule.coreConceptSummary: Legislative accountability refers to the constitutional mechanism through which the executive branch of government is held directly answerable to the elected legislature for its policies, actions, financial expenditures, and administrative performance. In India's parliamentary democracy, this relationship forms the bedrock of responsible governance, operationalized through instruments such as Question Hour, financial controls, and parliamentary committees.
highYieldFacts: Fact 1: Article 75(3) of the Constitution explicitly mandates that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

Fact 2: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC), established originally in 1921 under the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, is chaired by a member from the opposition, currently chosen by the Speaker to scrutinize Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) reports.
Fact 3: The Financial Committees of Parliament include the Public Accounts Committee (22 members), Estimates Committee (30 members), and Committee on Public Undertakings (22 members).

Fact 4: Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs), numbering 24, scrutinize demands for grants, bills, and policy initiatives of various ministries, operating as a vital mechanism for pre-legislative scrutiny.

Fact 5: The anti-defection law under the Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1985, often restricts free legislative voting and individual accountability due to strict party whips.
trapsAndElimination: Trap 1: Assuming the Estimates Committee includes members from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha; in reality, all 30 members of the Estimates Committee belong exclusively to the Lok Sabha.
Trap 2: Confusing collective responsibility (Article 75(3)) with individual ministerial responsibility (Article 75(2)), where ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
keyArticlesOrStatutes: Article 75(3) - Collective responsibility of the Executive to the Legislature
Articles 112-117 - Financial procedures and budgetary accountability
Tenth Schedule - Disqualification on ground of defection

mainsFramework.inDepthTheoryHtml:
Evolution and Constitutional Mandate of Legislative Accountability

Legislative accountability is the foundational pillar of the Westminster parliamentary model adopted by India. It transforms the democratic mandate into actionable governance by ensuring that the executive—vested with enormous administrative and coercive powers—remains under the continuous surveillance and control of the peoples representatives. Unlike the presidential system characterized by strict separation of powers and mutual checks, the parliamentary system fuses executive and legislative functions, making internal legislative oversight indispensable to prevent executive despotism.

Mechanisms of Legislative Scrutiny

The architecture of legislative accountability in India operates at multiple tiers:

  • Daily Accountability: Instruments like Question Hour, Zero Hour, Calling Attention Motions, and Half-an-Hour Discussions compel ministers to answer unannounced or specific policy queries on the floor of the House.
  • Financial Accountability: The annual budget process, cut motions, and post-expenditure audits by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) examined through the Public Accounts Committee ensure fiscal prudence and check misappropriation of public funds.
  • Institutional Oversight: The 24 Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) perform rigorous, closed-door scrutiny of legislative bills and budgetary allocations away from partisan political grandstanding.

Contemporary Structural Crises and Governance Deficits

Despite robust constitutional provisions, legislative accountability faces severe systemic decay in contemporary India.

  • Decline in Parliamentary Sitting Days: Parliaments across states and at the Centre have witnessed a steady decline in annual sitting days, frequently falling below 60-70 days a year, drastically truncating debate time.
  • Bypass of Committees: An increasing number of critical, complex bills are pushed through without reference to DRSCs or select committees, undermining expert scrutiny. For instance, landmark legislations are frequently passed as Money Bills or amidst pandemonium without substantive clause-by-clause discussion.
  • The Whip System and Anti-Defection: Paragraph 2(1)(b) of the Tenth Schedule forces MPs and MLAs to vote strictly along party lines, eroding individual legislative conscience and rendering floor accountability toothless against executive overreach.

dimensions.constitutional_or_legal: Interplay between Article 75(3), parliamentary privileges, rules of procedure, and the chilling effect of the anti-defection law on legislative independence.
dimensions.socio_economic: Failure to hold the executive accountable for welfare delivery, malnourishment, public health crises, and economic mismanagement due to truncated legislative debates.
dimensions.administrative_governance: Executive dominance over bureaucracy insulated by weak parliamentary oversight, leading to unchecked delegated legislation and arbitrary rule-making.
dimensions.international_or_comparative: Comparison with the UK Parliament's Prime Minister's Questions (PMQs) or the US Congressional Hearings, where executive officials face far more rigorous, non-partisan questioning.

landmarkJudgmentsOrReports: 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) - 14th Report on 'Strengthening Financial Management Systems'
National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC, 2002)
Supreme Court judgment in Kian Mohammadi v. State (on legislative privileges and transparency)

prelims.question: Which of the following is/are the function/functions of the Cabinet Secretariat?
options: 1. Preparation of agenda for Cabinet Meetings
3. Allocation of financial resources to the Ministries
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
prelims.explanation: The Cabinet Secretariat is responsible for the administration of the Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1961, and Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961, facilitating smooth transaction of business in cabinets and committees. Allocation of financial resources is done by the Ministry of Finance, not the Cabinet Secretariat.

mains.question: To what extent, in your view, has the Parliament been able to ensure accountability of the executive in India? Discuss the institutional impediments it faces.

modelMainsQA.question: Examine the effectiveness of legislative committees as instruments of legislative accountability in India. What structural and procedural bottlenecks impede their functioning? (150 Words, 10 Marks)

approach.intro: Define legislative accountability and highlight the central role of Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) as mini-parliaments.
approach.body: Analyze their effectiveness in detailed scrutiny, expert consultations, and non-partisan debates. Highlight structural bottlenecks such as declining referral of bills, lack of domain expertise among MPs, short tenures, and attendance issues.
approach.conclusion: Suggest systemic reforms including mandatory pre-legislative scrutiny, mandatory committee vetting of bills, and capacity building to restore legislative supremacy.

modelMainsQA.modelAnswerHtml:
Legislative accountability forms the lifeblood of India's parliamentary democracy, operationalized primarily through Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs). Functioning as 'mini-parliaments', these 24 committees scrutinize demands for grants, policies, and legislative bills away from the political polarization of the floor.

Effectiveness of Legislative Committees:

  • Deep Scrutiny: Unlike the chaotic floor of the House, committees conduct clause-by-clause analysis and take depositions from domain experts, civil society, and bureaucratic stakeholders.
  • Consensus Building: Operating behind closed doors sans media glare, committee reports are typically consensual, bridging partisan divides (e.g., stellar reports on crucial economic and social bills).
  • Fiscal Oversight: Examination of departmental budgets ensures accountability in public expenditure and curbs executive high-handedness.

Structural and Procedural Bottlenecks:

  • Decline in Referrals: The proportion of bills referred to DRSCs has plummeted sharply in recent years; critical economic and criminal legislations are frequently pushed through without committee scrutiny.
  • Short Tenure and Attendance: Committees suffer from frequent re-constitutions (annual rotation), interrupting institutional memory, alongside poor attendance of parliamentarians.
  • Lack of Independent Research Support: Unlike the US Congressional Research Service, Indian committees lack dedicated, independent research wings to counter executive data dominance.

Way Forward:
To rejuvenate legislative accountability, reference of all major bills to DRSCs must be made constitutionally or procedurally mandatory. Empowering committees with independent expert research support and extending their tenure will insulate governance from executive overreach, upholding constitutional morality.

practiceMCQs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament: 
1. It examines the finance accounts and audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG).
2. A minister is not eligible to be elected as a member of the Committee.
3. The Chairman of the Committee is invariably appointed from the ruling party by the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceMCQs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: PAC scrutinizes appropriation accounts and CAG audit reports. Statement 2 is correct: Ministers cannot be elected to financial committees as they cannot audit themselves. Statement 3 is incorrect: Since 1967, by convention, the Chairman of the PAC is invariably chosen from the opposition party in the Lok Sabha.

practiceMCQs.question: Which of the following constitutional provisions directly establishes executive responsibility to the legislature in India?
practiceMCQs.explanation: Article 75(3) of the Constitution explicitly states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha), which is the constitutional anchor of legislative accountability in India.
